info.name: Enterprise Collaboration Platform API
info.description:
Covers every endpoint implemented through Week 3-4 (Section 4 of the requirement doc): Auth, Users, Organizations, Workspaces, Projects, Tasks, Comments, Notifications, Attachments, plus a folder demonstrating RBAC enforcement (401/403) and a final destructive Cleanup folder.

**Setup**
1. `docker compose up -d postgres redis`
2. `npm run prisma:migrate -w apps/api`
3. `npm run dev -w apps/api` (listens on http://localhost:3000, prefix `/api/v1`)
4. Run this collection top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner, or work through folders individually - each folder captures the ids it creates into collection variables (`{{organizationId}}`, `{{workspaceId}}`, `{{projectId}}`, `{{taskId}}`, `{{commentId}}`) for the next folder to reuse.

**Recommended order**: Auth -> Users -> Organizations -> Workspaces -> Projects -> Tasks -> Comments -> Notifications -> Attachments -> RBAC Examples -> Cleanup (Destructive). The Cleanup folder is last on purpose - it deletes the resources created above, so run it only when you're done exploring.

**Re-runnable by design**: `Register`, `Register (Invitee)`, `Create Organization`, and `Create Workspace` regenerate a fresh random email/slug in their Pre-request Script on every single execution (never reused across runs). That means the whole collection can be run via the Collection Runner as many times as you want, back to back, even if a previous run's Cleanup folder was skipped or failed partway - each run always creates its own brand-new user, org, and workspace instead of colliding with (or pointing at stale ids from) an earlier run. `Register`'s Pre-request Script also clears any same-named keys from the active Postman **Environment** first, since Environment variables take precedence over Collection variables in Postman - so a leftover `accessToken`/`refreshToken`/etc. saved in an Environment from earlier manual testing can never shadow the fresh values this run produces.

**Running the whole collection in one go**: use the Collection Runner (or Run button) and select the collection root, not an individual folder, so every folder executes in the order below in a single run. If you want the run to keep going and show you every result even when a step fails, make sure the Runner's *(Postman app version-dependent, roughly)* "Stop run on error" / "Halt on test failure" toggle is left OFF - it's off by default. Do not select a saved Environment that predates this collection unless you're sure it doesn't define `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `organizationId`, `workspaceId`, `projectId`, `taskId`, or `commentId` - "No Environment" is the simplest safe choice since this collection is fully self-contained via Collection variables.

Every success response is wrapped by the API's global interceptor as `{ success, statusCode, data }`; tests below read `data` accordingly. The Attachments folder's Upload Attachment request needs a file manually attached to exercise the full upload/download/delete flow when run interactively in the Postman app - running it unattended (Collection Runner/newman) without one is expected and still passes (the request is written to accept either outcome). Two accounts are used throughout: the primary caller (`{{accessToken}}`, ends up OWNER of the org/workspace) and an invitee (`{{inviteeAccessToken}}`, added as a VIEWER) used to demonstrate RBAC denial in the RBAC Examples folder.

body.raw:
{
  "title": "Set up CI pipeline",
  "description": "Run lint, unit, and e2e tests on every PR.",
  "priority": "HIGH",
  "dueDate": "2026-12-31T00:00:00.000Z",
  "labels": ["backend", "infra"],
  "assigneeId": "{{inviteeUserId}}"
}

request.description: MEMBER or above. The assignee must already be a workspace member - run Workspaces > Invite/Update Member first.
Supports ?status=&priority=&assigneeId=&sort=&page=&limit= (sort accepts createdAt|dueDate|priority|status|title, optionally prefixed with '-' for descending).
MEMBER or above. Status must follow TODO -> IN_PROGRESS -> REVIEW -> DONE; a new task starts at TODO, so this is the one legal next step.
The task is currently IN_PROGRESS, so the only legal next status is REVIEW - jumping straight to DONE must be rejected.
ADMIN or OWNER only. Soft delete - see Restore Task below, which reverses this so the task stays usable for the Comments/Attachments folders.
ADMIN or OWNER only. Reverses Delete Task (Soft).
MEMBER or above.
Only the comment's own author may edit it, regardless of workspace role.
Only the comment's own author may delete it, regardless of workspace role. Soft delete - see Restore Comment (Own) below.
Only the comment's own author may restore it. Reverses Delete Comment (Own).
Assigns the task to the caller (not the invitee, unlike the Tasks folder's example) specifically so a TASK_ASSIGNED notification lands in the caller's own inbox for the next request to find.

Notification delivery is asynchronous (BullMQ), so a notification from the request above may or may not have been processed yet by the time this runs - this only asserts the response shape, never a specific count, so it stays reliable on every run regardless of queue timing.

item.name: [404] Mark a Non-Existent Notification as Read

request.description: Deterministic by design (a random guid can never match a real row), rather than depending on the async notification above having landed yet. Demonstrates the ownership/not-found check: markRead() 404s for any id that isn't both real and owned by the caller.

formdata.description: Running interactively in the Postman app? Click here and select a small file (e.g. a PDF, image, or .txt) to exercise the full upload/list/download/delete flow below. Running unattended (Collection Runner / newman) with no file selected is expected and still passes - the request below is written to handle both outcomes.

request.description: MEMBER or above. Size/MIME are validated server-side (UPLOAD_MAX_SIZE_MB, an image/PDF/office/text/zip allow-list). File upload can't be scripted through collection variables the way JSON bodies can - see the 'file' field description for what to do when running this by hand.

request.description: Captures a separate token for the invitee account (VIEWER in the workspace), used by the negative tests below without disturbing the primary {{accessToken}}.
No Authorization header is sent. The global JwtAuthGuard should reject this before it reaches the controller.
Creating a project requires MEMBER or above; the invitee is only a VIEWER, so RolesGuard must reject with 403.
Deleting a workspace requires OWNER; the invitee is only a VIEWER, so RolesGuard must reject with 403. Nothing is deleted, so the Cleanup folder still works afterward.

item.name: Cleanup (Destructive)
item.description: Deletes the resources this collection created. Deliberately placed last and ordered child-first (Task -> Project -> Workspace -> Organization) so earlier folders keep working if you re-run them. Skip this folder if you want to keep exploring the data in Swagger/pgAdmin.
